title: Embedded Relational Database Engine with Slotted-Page B-Tree & WAL
problem: Software engineers interact with relational databases daily through high-level SQL queries, yet the underlying execution mechanisms—slotted page on-disk record serialization, buffer pool frame eviction, B-tree balance maintenance through page splits, and Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) for crash recovery—remain opaque black boxes. Building an embedded storage engine from first principles demystifies how relational data survives unexpected system crashes without page corruption. This project implements a self-contained embedded database engine in C++ featuring a slotted-page disk manager, an LRU-K buffer pool, a B-tree clustered index, a Volcano-style iterator query executor, and ARIES-style write-ahead logging.
use_cases: Embedded edge persistence for Internet of Things gateways and autonomous devices
High-reliability local transaction logs for financial point-of-sale terminals
Specialized telemetry storage engines requiring deterministic crash recovery
hard_parts: Managing slotted-page layout with variable-length tuple offsets and in-place fragment compaction
Implementing thread-safe B-tree node splits, merges, and root page re-allocations during concurrency
Synchronizing buffer pool dirty frame flushing with Write-Ahead Log sequence numbers (WAL protocol)
Executing ARIES crash recovery phases (Analysis, Redo, and Undo) to restore ACID consistency
screener_signals: Modular C++ implementation cleanly separating storage, buffer pool, indexing, parser, and recovery
Automated crash-kill test verifying zero committed transaction loss across 10 unexpected SIGKILL terminations
Anti-fake verification script inserting dynamic nonces, terminating process mid-write, and asserting recovery

stack.role: systems programming language for disk manager, buffer pool, B-tree index, and WAL

components.name: Slotted Page Disk Manager
components.purpose: Manages 4KB database page allocation on disk, tuple offset arrays, and free space compaction

components.name: LRU-K Buffer Pool Manager
components.purpose: Pins frequently accessed pages in memory and evicts unpinned frames using backward k-distance

components.name: B-Tree Index Manager
components.purpose: Provides logarithmic search, leaf insertion, and node splitting for indexed primary keys

components.name: Volcano Query Executor
components.purpose: Executes SELECT, INSERT, and WHERE filter query plans using open-next-close iterator models

components.name: Write-Ahead Log & Recovery Manager
components.purpose: Appends transaction log records before writing dirty pages and performs crash recovery

architecture.data_flow: SQL queries enter the Volcano Query Executor; the executor requests index scans from the B-Tree Index Manager; the B-Tree manager requests page IDs from the LRU-K Buffer Pool; the buffer pool fetches unpinned 4KB frames from the Slotted Page Disk Manager; updates append transaction records to the Write-Ahead Log before dirty pages are flushed to disk; on unexpected crash, the Recovery Manager reads WAL records sequentially to reconstruct uncommitted transactions and restore consistency.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Page latch pins preventing buffer eviction during active access; WAL sequence numbers strictly enforced prior to flushing dirty memory frames.

targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, Linux filesystem with POSIX fsync

targets.target: Recovery reconstructs 20 of 20 committed batches with 0 corrupted slotted pages

prerequisites: Proficiency in modern C++ (pointers, memory management, RAII, std::unique_ptr)
Understanding of operating system paging, POSIX file I/O (open, lseek, fsync), and binary byte buffers

environment.accounts_keys_quotas: No external cloud accounts, paid services, or API keys required
environment.reference_environment: Local 4-core CPU with GCC 11+ or Clang 13+ installed
environment.fallback_path: Standard POSIX file operations with in-memory page simulation if direct disk fsync encounters permission limits

riskiest_component.name: Page Corruption During Incomplete B-Tree Node Splits
riskiest_component.fallback: Implement shadow-page copy-on-write during leaf split before atomically publishing parent pointer

worksheet.q1: Core deliverable: an embedded C++ relational storage engine with slotted-page layout, LRU-K buffer pool, B-tree index, Volcano query engine, and WAL crash recovery.
worksheet.q2: Target users: systems software engineers, edge runtime developers, and database infrastructure specialists.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: edge device persistence, point-of-sale transaction logs, and telemetry storage engines.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 41 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 36 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 41.4 -> 41 hours. Advanced level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: slotted page tuple compaction, thread-safe B-tree node splits, WAL dirty frame flushing synchronization, and ARIES recovery phases.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: 100,000 structured relational rows with integer keys. No personal data.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Fallback: POSIX file I/O with in-memory page simulation.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: Page corruption during incomplete B-tree leaf splits. Fallback: shadow-page copy-on-write during split.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: mock query returns without disk access. Anti-fake check 5 inserts dynamic uncommitted nonce, aborts, and asserts zero leakage.
worksheet.q10: Safety/ethics: Safe; synthetic relational test records only.
